LESSON: SIGN READING 7.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Sign Reading 7.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 7.2.1 Fluency, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to sign read words fluently?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 7.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learner: The learner’s ability to learn independently is enhanced as they practise sign reading sentences containing decodable and non- decodable words for sign reading fluency.

Values:
Responsibility is developed as learner acquires self-drive and practises sign reading fluently on their own.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: Social cohesion as the learner participates in a readers theatre with peers.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Fluency is applied when sign reading texts in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as Hearing aids and amplifiers, charts showing words with the target letter sounds, flash cards

showing words with target letter sound, signed audio-visual recordings, print or digital stories, pocket charts, print and digital flash cards.
